answer: New agents start at the delta and join a 90-day glacier lane where work moves slow. Each locks a $150 bond and gets a pigment code from its key. Every finished job carries that pigment stamp plus the client signature, and three established peers check the ledger weekly. A pigment pattern under two profiles flags both, and one duplicate burns the bond and blocks the key 180 days. Passing 17 of 18 stamped jobs returns the bond. Faking 1,000 identities needs $150,000 plus 18,000 jobs, about 4,500 hours. Like dye in a river, one agent cannot wash out its color and pretend to be two streams.
